title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Extended features are what turn a working plasma computer into a universal one: networking between machines, self-repair of damaged cells, security for wave channels, and the architectural headroom to keep growing. Each feature is a real engineering discipline borrowed from conventional computing and re-expressed in plasma: packets become soliton trains, firewalls become field barriers, backups become spheromak archives.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Networking plasma machines
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Machines link two ways: fiber optics carrying conventional packets between I/O ports, and — more radically — coupled plasma volumes sharing waves directly through field bridges. The network stack mirrors the internet's layers: solitons as packets, density channels as links, routing by field-steered waveguides. Latency between racks is microseconds; bandwidth per link is gigabits. Distributed plasma computing is then a straightforward extension of distributed conventional computing.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Self-repair and cell regeneration
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. A damaged cell — contaminated, unstable, or simply faded — can be healed: pump it out, re-ionize fresh gas, re-establish the field bottle, and reload its state from a neighbor or the archive tier. Because the medium is a gas, 'replacing the hardware' is a software operation. Biological inspiration is explicit: the machine regrows tissue the way bodies heal, and the repair controller is modeled on immune response — detect, isolate, regenerate.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Fault isolation and containment of failures
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. A runaway instability in one cell must not cascade: field barriers between cell groups act as firebreaks, absorbing or reflecting rogue waves, and the containment AI quarantines suspect regions by raising their bottle walls. This is defense in depth — the same principle as bulkheads in ships and availability zones in clouds. The failure contract: any single cell may die; the machine may not.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Security for wave channels
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Wave channels can be intercepted — a probe near a density channel reads the traffic — so plasma networking needs cryptography like any network: encrypted payloads, authenticated endpoints, and key exchange over the same I/O ports. The medium offers one exotic defense: spread-spectrum wave encoding that hides signals below the thermal noise floor, readable only with the spreading code. Security here is conventional crypto plus physics-flavored stealth.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Scaling toward universality
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Universality is a checklist, not a feeling: Turing-complete logic (have it, via NOR), unbounded memory (have it, via tiered plasma memory), I/O (have it), networking (have it), and the ability to simulate any other computer (emulation layer). The extended-features program marches down that list, verifying each item with tests. When every box is checked and demonstrated, the plasma computer is universal in the same sense as any other: it can compute anything computable.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — Hybrid operation with conventional systems
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The plasma computer will not replace silicon overnight; it will accelerate it. Hybrid operation pairs plasma wave-processors with conventional hosts over fast interconnects: the host handles control flow and the plasma handles wave-native kernels. This is the GPU model replayed — and GPUs won exactly this way. The extended feature is the runtime: it schedules kernels, moves data, and hides the physics behind a familiar accelerator API.

title: Plasma Computer Extended Features — The road to the universal machine
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The full roadmap runs: single certified cell, tiled array, networked modules, hybrid datacenter, and finally the universal plasma facility. Each stage reuses the previous stage's pieces — generation, containment, logic, memory, I/O, power — and adds one extended feature. The teaching ladder mirrors it: students progress from one cell to the universe of machines. Nothing in the extended set requires new physics; it requires the engineering will to assemble what the piece databases already describe.
